job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: In the bustling town of Ooty, two friends, Arjun and Meera, decided to track their daily habits using simple charts. Arjun spent 45 minutes every morning watering his garden, while Meera spent 60 minutes practicing the sitar. To compare their progress, they drew a bar graph. A bar graph is a visual tool where the height of the bars represents the amount of time spent on an activity. Because Arjun wanted to see his plants grow faster, he increased his watering time to 75 minutes. Meanwhile, Meera noticed that her fingers felt stiff after long practice sessions, so she reduced her time to 40 minutes. On the 12th of March, they looked at their graph to see the changes. Arjun realized that the taller bar on his side of the graph showed his increased effort. The graph helped them understand their schedules clearly. While Arjun focused on his garden, Meera realized that the graph was not just for plants, but for any activity that can be measured. They both agreed that visual data makes it much easier to spot trends than reading a long list of numbers.
response.summary: Arjun and Meera use bar graphs to track the time they spend on their daily hobbies. The visual representation helps them compare their progress and understand their schedule changes over time.
